subject.title: feat(wizard): deliver progress over the RPC wizard protocol

question: Should `progress` steps be backward-tolerant for clients that still answer them, or should this PR intentionally require every RPC wizard client to re-poll without an answer before progress frames are emitted broadly?
rationale: The schema already permits `progress`, but current bundled clients answer progress-capable steps and the PR makes those ids unanswerable; choosing the permanent protocol compatibility contract needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve progress-answering clients
options.body: Tolerate progress answers server-side or update bundled clients before broad emission so current clients do not fail during setup.

options.title: Accept a client contract break
options.body: Land the non-answerable progress contract only if maintainers intentionally require all clients to switch to re-polling without an answer and have rollout proof.

options.title: Pause behind the umbrella issue
options.body: Keep this PR paused until the broader wizard RPC parity contract in the canonical issue settles progress semantics.

recommendation.title: Preserve progress-answering clients
recommendation.body: Tolerate progress answers server-side or update bundled clients before broad emission so current clients do not fail during setup.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this person to the original wizard/onboarding path and the current Crestodian client that would be affected by the progress-step contract.
